why: L-CAD-08: the round section a plan note states, read off the strings F-RCC6-BNBC really draws — `C7 %%C450 PORCH COLUMN` (S-10, handle 9BA) and `89 NOS. %%C500 BORED PILES` (S-02) — one token at a time. The sign stands at an END of the text or the text states no diameter: a note read whole would take a diameter out of prose, so every sentence here answers null. `16%%C` answers a diameter of sixteen because the string does say a circle of sixteen; what makes it a bar rather than a section is the column it stands under, not the glyph, and that is the caller's question. Every case is the fixture's own save the two sign-after forms (`450Ø`, `450 MM DIA`), which pin that a diameter takes its unit exactly as a side of a pair does (L-MEA-01: a figure nobody gave a unit to keeps none).
